newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LatAm stocks seen keeping bullish tone in week.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen keeping bullish tone in week.

text.p: Latin American bourses were expected to continue rising on local factors this week with only Mexico still glued to Wall Street, dealers said.
In Chile, brokers saw shares extending their record-breaking bull run mainly on strong foreign buying, although the rally could be tempered by profit-taking.
The blue-chip .IPSA rose 3.7 percent last week to end at 129.89 points Friday.

Traders attributed recent gains to prospects for better economic growth during the rest of the year without inflation, a likely cut in interest rates in June or July, and an end to a severe drought in central Chile. Water shortages had forced electricity companies to spend more on fossil fuels to make up for lost hydroelectric output at dams.
"The bolsa is on very good footing, as volume levels show," said one broker. Turnover has swelled to the year's highest levels, with 220 million shares traded Friday.
In Argentina, stocks were also seen building on recent strong gains, which have pushed the blue-chip MerVal index .MERV to a five-year high.

"The market is close to its near-term targets but some stocks may continue to rise selectively this week, based on recent corporate news, pushing the index further up," said Luis Corsiglia of brokers Corsiglia y Cia.

The MerVal rose 1.4 percent last week to 778.08 and closed 7.7 percent higher in May. The bolsa was boosted last week by news of purchases by foreign groups of leading local banks and by other corporate activity involving blue-chip companies.
In Venezuela share prices were seen firming in a high-profile week in which prime oil fields are due to be auctioned and expected to attract high bids.

In addition, the Senate may vote Wednesday on crucial labor reforms which have been steadily working their way through Congress. "Everything is looking good ... it all depends on the news. Labor reform approval would be very positive for the market," said Hector Perez at brokers Union.
Last week the bolsa's 19-share .IBC rose 1.6 percent to close Friday at 6,855.41 points, underpinned by continuing foreign interest in blue chips.

Brazilian shares were seen steady to higher this week, awaiting a key vote in Congress on a telecommunications law and Wednesday's release of the names of qualified bidders for the much-awaited Band B cellular selloff, brokers said.
Shares, boosted by increased foreign and local buy orders, have rallied recently on expectations that bids presented by consortia interested in the Band B were exceptionally high.

However, some traders noted the market could follow the bolsa's "buy on the rumor, sell on the fact" rule and take a breather after Wednesday's announcement. Also, the sharp rally could prompt investors to take profits.
Last week the leading Bovespa index .BVSP rose 5.3 pct, ending Friday at 11345 points. In May it climbed 13.6 and it stands 61.1 percent higher so far this year.
Stockwatchers in Mexico said they would resume careful observation of U.S. economic data for signs of possible tightening of monetary policy at the July Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

"The exchange rate and domestic interest rates will become more relevant, depending on how they react to U.S. data," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy. Analysts were divided as to whether share prices had significant upside potential before the next FOMC meeting.
Mexico's blue chip IPC .MXX index shed 22.28 points, or 0.5 percent, last week to 3,988.29 after a rough ride on the back of U.S. market volatility and disappointing domestic economic data.
